text:
ana (PM): Folks — for the PRD I need a concise enumeration of edge cases we must cover for the generation API (streaming, truncation, token limits, retries). Can we list them and propose acceptance criteria? Keeping it customer-focused (SLOs + UX).

michael (eng): Starting list: streaming partial outputs + reconnects, truncated response when user hits token limit, stop-sequence vs truncation ambiguity, retry dedup & idempotency, high-latency backpressure causing partial streams, client-side aborted connections, streaming + function-calls where call payload sent mid-stream.

tara (ml): Add model-level behaviors: hallucination spikes near length limit, sudden EOS token emission when kv-cache full, variable tokenization edge cases (emoji, unicode), sampling changes when batching mixes prompt lengths.

liam (platform): Also infra: GPU OOM during streaming, partial chunk persisted in cache, retry amplification on transient infra failures, and cross-region fallback affecting model variant (different tokenizer or quantization).

ana (PM): @michael @tara @liam can we map each to an acceptance criterion? e.g., what counts as "handled" vs "deferred" for launch?

michael (eng): I'll propose short ACs: 1) Streaming reconnect: client can resume from last acked token; server supports resume token within 30s window; if resume impossible, server sends explicit "incomplete_truncation=true" metadata. 2) Truncation reporting: if response truncated due to token limit, API returns a structured flag in final metadata: {"truncated":true, "reason":"token_limit"} and a recommended retry strategy. 3) Retry idempotency: generation requests include a client-provided idempotency_key; retries within 10m must not produce duplicate external side-effects (function calls).

michael (eng): 4) Stop-seq vs truncation: if stop-seq encountered, stream closes with code 0 and metadata {"stop_sequence":"<seq>"}. If truncated due to length, metadata as above. 5) Streaming+function-calls: partial function payload should be buffered server-side until complete function call message; clients must not execute incomplete payloads.

tara (ml): ACs for quality: 6) Pre-emptive quality drop: if model detects likely degenerative sampling near limit, emit warning token in meta and allow client to request safety-boosted decoding (slower but lower randomness). 7) Tokenization sanity: API will provide token_count() endpoint for the same tokenizer used server-side so clients can pre-check lengths.

liam (platform): Infra ACs: 8) OOM handling: on GPU OOM mid-stream, server should fail the request with metadata {"failure_mode":"oom","can_retry":true/false} plus suggestion to downgrade model or quantization. 9) Cross-region fallback: requests routed to fallback region must include model_version compatibility check; if incompatible, return 409 with convertible-variants list.

ana (PM): Great. Now prioritization: which of these are "must-have" for GA vs "nice-to-have"? My proposal: Must-have: 1,2,3,4,8 (resume/explicit truncation/reporting/idempotency/oom handling). Nice-to-have: 5,6,7,9. Thoughts?

michael (eng): Agree, + make 5 (function-call buffering) stretch target for GA if we can guarantee no-execution of partial payloads; otherwise must-have for enterprise customers.

 tara (ml): For 6 (quality warning), we can ship a lightweight heuristic first (prob threshold) as a GA flag but make the safety-boosted decoding opt-in for Dedicated/Private initially.

liam (platform): Implementation notes: resume token requires storing per-request append-only stream state for 30s — cost estimate: ~X GB/day per 1k concurrent streams. Can reduce to 10s window for hosted GA to limit cost. Also OOM metadata needs standard error schema across runtime.

ana (PM): Good call. Let's set launch criteria: - All must-have ACs implemented and tested in staging. - End-to-end customer scenario tests: client reconnects and resumes stream (automated), client observes truncation flag and retries, idempotency key prevents duplicate function calls. - Instrumentation: metrics for truncated_count, resume_success_rate, retry_duplicates.

michael (eng): Tests: unit tests for resume token encoding/decoding, integration test simulating partial stream + reconnect, chaos test for GPU OOM during generation to verify metadata and safe retry path.

liam (platform): Rollout plan: feature-flag streaming-resume and truncation-metadata. Progressive rollout to 10% hosted, then Dedicated customers opt-in, monitor resume_success_rate > 95% and no user-visible duplicate function calls.

ana (PM): Scope negotiation: if we only have bandwidth for 3 items, implement: truncation metadata, retry/idempotency, and OOM failure metadata. Defer resume-window to post-GA if cost too high. Is that acceptable?

michael (eng): Acceptable trade. Will draft short RFC with ACs and test plan. I'll add sample API responses and client pseudocode for resume + truncation handling.

deploy-bot: Deployed draft RFC (rfc/1763600000-streaming-edgecases) to docs for review — please comment within 48h. :rocket:

ana (PM): Thanks team — please add any missing edge-cases now. I'll incorporate into PRD and set priorities for the next roadmap sync. :thumbsup:
